content.text: ▪︎back pain: most cases self-limited - 90% resolve w.in 6wks of tx
▪︎malig: unexplained wt loss · failure to improve w tx · pain >6wks · pain @ rest or night + hx of CA or age >50 → further w/u
▪︎infect/epidural abscess: fever · pain @ rest · recent infect or surg · immunocompromised · IVDU
▪︎back pain + fever + neuro deficits: epidural abscess
▪︎other serious Eti of back pain: AAA or dissection · PUD · kidney stones · pyelonephritis · pancreatitis
▪︎nonopioid tx 1st-line for nonspecific musc back pain
▪︎strain of cervical paraspinal musc - often hx of minor precipitating inj but can occur from everyday stressors (poor posture or sleep habits)
▪︎PE: tenderness of neck paraspinal + trapezius musc w.o radicular sx - full but painful ROM
▪︎⍉neuro deficits or extremity weakness → if present, w/u other Eti

▪︎red flags: recent major trauma · weakness · gait chgs · bowel or bladder dysfx · Lhermitte phenomenon · fever or chills · IVDU · IS · unexplained wt loss · hx of CA · visual chgs · anterior neck pain
▪︎XR ⍉recommended for acute nontraumatic neck pain - XR if persistent mod–severe pain >6wks or interferes w sleep · work or ADLs
▪︎MRI: red flags · mod–severe pain ⍉responding to conservative mgmt in 6wks or progress neuro dysfx
▪︎most mild–mod strains resolve w conservative mgmt over 6wks - pain + stiffness can last up to 6wks
▪︎conservative: pt education + reassurance · home exercise program · heat or cold · posture modification (sitting/standing - sleep w neck aligned w body)
▪︎home exercise: early mobilization + gentle stretching to maintain ROM
▪︎nonbenzodiazepine skeletal muscle relaxant: sx ⍉controlled w nonopioid analgesics or cervical spasm
▪︎tramadol: only if inadeq control w NSAIDs · APAP or muscle relaxants - never initial tx
▪︎prednisone: ⍉a recommended tx for acute neck pain
▪︎inj to a musculotendinous unit - often from violent contract or excessive stretching
▪︎grade 1: minor fiber tearing · mild tenderness or swelling · minimal fx loss
▪︎grade 2: partial tearing · mod pain · swelling · bruising · strength loss
▪︎grade 3: complete tear w separation of musc or tendon - poss palpable defect or avulsion frx
▪︎localized pain · swelling · bruising · loss of fx
▪︎pain ↑ w musc use · stretching or direct pressure
▪︎complete rupture: may have visible or palpable musc deformity
▪︎intercostal strain: tenderness over the musc - ↑ w stretching it (ex deep breath)
▪︎US or MRI to confirm complete tears (esp complex or delayed cases)
▪︎grade 1–2: rest · ice · NSAIDs · gradual return to activity
▪︎grade 3: ED mgmt + early ortho Refer - some need surg repair or immobilization
▪︎early mobilization once pain allows full ROM + musc use
